A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AGPD by the same authors. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, added, and removed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments on CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, and GTSRB, including attack comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original detection experiments, including revised benchmark results, DTD and ImageNet evaluations, separation analyses, and an ASSET architecture experiment.

M1.justification: V2 substantially revises filtering: v1 removes samples with high min-max-normalized scores and stops at a fixed CVBT reduction; v2 removes samples with low clean-reference closeness and selects a stopping iteration retrospectively using JS divergence and a sliding-window objective. CVBT also gains class-size normalization. These change the procedure, beyond its retained three-stage framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds DTD textures and ImageNet-200, plus CTRL attack evaluation and a five-trigger scenario replacing the paired-trigger scenarios. CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, GTSRB, and OOD clean-reference testing were already present. LC detection rows disappear, although its appendix GCD visualization remains; GTSRB coverage loses LF, SSBA, and TaCT evaluations.

E2.justification: The main comparisons remove D-ST and FREAK and add ABL, CD, and ASSET. The multi-target comparison expands from STRIP and SCAn to eight detectors. Poisoning-ratio plots replace Beatrix and Spectral with STRIP and ABL, while the clean-reference sensitivity experiment drops its SCAn comparison.

E3.justification: V2 replaces weighted F1 with standard F1 throughout the evaluations. Its stated poisoning protocol distinguishes 10% for non-clean-label attacks and 5% for clean-label attacks, whereas v1 states a general 10%. Multi-trigger allocations change from two 5% components to five 2% components. V2 also adds a ResNet18 control for ASSET. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative silhouette comparisons (Table 3), a TP/FP/JS-divergence stopping trace (Figure 7), ASSET architecture sensitivity (Appendix J), and t-SNE case analyses (Appendix K). Its threshold analysis replaces v1's p, tau, and xi sweeps with a tau_s sweep. Existing GCD illustrations and clean-reference/OOD analyses are retained or updated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations for runtime and selected sensitivity or gradient summaries. Neither provides detection seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's sliding-window standard deviation is part of its stopping algorithm, not a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerous detection values and analysis results change. In the shared CIFAR-10/PreActResNet18/BadNets setting, Table 1 reports AGPD TPR/FPR changing from 98.24%/0.44% to 90.06%/0.03%. V2 adds dataset, silhouette, stopping-trace, and ASSET-control results, while removing v1's VGG19-BN multi-target results. Weighted-F1 versus F1 values and averages over changed attack sets are not directly comparable.

T1.justification: Mathematical revisions concern definitions and algorithmic rules: CVBT changes from a root sum to a root mean square with a stated [0,2] bound, the Z-score numerator loses its absolute value, and Appendix E defines the new window-selection objective. V1's asymptotic complexity expressions are removed. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim remains gradient-based poisoned-sample detection through target-class identification and filtering. V2 expands the stated contributions from the dispersion observation and CVBT to two explicit observations and two metrics, promoting within-class clean/poison separation and sample closeness into the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism explanation for JS-based stopping, detailed interpretations of input- and loss-based detectors' failures, ASSET's architecture dependence, and a scalability limitation from scanning model layers. It also drops v1's explicit qualification that WaNet and Input-Aware evaluation assumes knowledge of their training methods, reducing clarity about applicability.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset-size and architecture tables, batch sizes, training settings for additional datasets, RTX A5000 hardware information, and stopping-window parameters. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. Conversely, v1's code-access link and learning-rate scheduler details disappear. Appendix F specifies ResNet50 for ImageNet, but Table 10 names PreActResNet18, leaving that setting unresolved.

R1.justification: Related work is revised around activation-, input-, and loss-based detection, adding discussion or citations for CD, ASSET, CTRL, silhouette analysis, and datasets. Several earlier references, including SantiNet, LIRA, and Marksman, disappear. The central positioning of AGPD as an activation-gradient alternative to existing detection approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around two observations. V2 separates GCD preliminaries from the detection method, reorganizes the algorithm into explicit stages, restructures experiments and appendices, and adds a limitations paragraph. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the pipeline, restructures comparison tables, combines analyses into Figure 5, and relocates VGG results and activation-distribution analysis to appendices. New dataset, silhouette, stopping-trace, and t-SNE displays are added. Both appendix GCD images are retained unchanged despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the central separation argument with quantitative silhouette evidence and adds broader comparisons, including an ASSET architecture control. Its filtering inequality now agrees with the displayed closeness score, and the revised stopping rule is explicitly specified. These gains are tempered by lost code and scheduler information, a dropped training-access qualification, and contradictory ImageNet backbone descriptions in Appendix F and Table 10, limiting the net improvement.
